DISCUSSION ITEMS a.
Review of the Enacted Budget Vice President Abby Benson noted that the official State budget has not been approved yet.
She provided a brief overview of the University’s FY25 Budget request, specifically the requests for an operating budget increase, Rhode Island Capital Plan Fund (RICAP), and a Biomedical Sciences Building General Obligation (GO) Bond.
With respect to the operating budget increases, she noted that URI requested a $32.1M increase, the legislature recommended a $5.4M increase.
With respect to RICAP asset protection funding, she noted that URI requested $16.3M, the legislature recommended $14.0M.
With respect to the Biomedical Sciences GO Bond, she noted that URI requested $87.45M, the legislature recommended $87.5M.
She provided additional detail regarding the operating budget increase request and the RICAP request (specifically related to PFAS remediation efforts).

Responding to questions, Vice President Benson noted that budget shortfalls are traditionally managed though the use of reserves to meet contractual obligations and also that the pending new budget model will allow the University to clearly evaluate and reset the University’s budget.
She also noted that the appropriation from the state is roughly 20% of the University’s education and general budget. b.
Report of Actions Taken in Executive Session Briar Lane Acquisition Enclosure Vice President Benson reported the action taken in Executive Session by the Board of Trustees Finance and Facilities Committee on April 4, 2024, and by the Board of Trustees on April 26, 2024, to approve the acquisition of property at 63 Briar Lane, Kingston, RI.
She noted that, following the Board’s approval in April, the University is currently completing the purchase of this property. 3.

TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Facilities Committee FROM: Abby Benson, Vice President for Administration and Finance DATE: June 10, 2024 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of Repairs to the President’s Residence Purpose of Submittal: Per the President’s contract, the “University will provide maintenance, utilities, and insurance for the Residence and the surrounding grounds in accordance with its normal and customary practices.
All additions, remodeling, or equipment purchases for the Residence in excess of $10,000 will be subject to the Board's prior approval. ” This item seeks approval from the Board of Trustees for replacement of the Residence outside deck, which is expected to exceed $10,000.
Recommendation: I recommend approval of this item.

Points to Consider: The Facilities Group has made several minor repairs to the Residence deck in recent years, but has determined that the entire structure needs to be replaced to ensure continued safe use.
The deck is used frequently to host community events at the Residence.
This project, anticipated to occur during the summer 2024, would include replacement of all structural components and all decking and railings, as well as associated modifications and repairs to the Residence itself as needed.
The Facilities Group is currently seeking updated quotes for this work, but based on quotes received last year, anticipates spending no more than $50,000 on this project.
Supporting Information: None Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT, the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the repair and/or replacement of the outside deck to the President’s Residence as presented, at a cost of no more than $50,000.

Definitions.

Amendments to the Memorandum of Understanding .

Recommendation: I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve of renewal and extension of URI’s contract with Oracle America as presented on substantially the terms in the enclosed term sheet, and that any authorized signatory (as defined in the Policy on Approval and Execution of Contracts and Other Binding Documents) be authorized to negotiate the terms of any documents relating to such transaction on substantially the terms in the enclosure, with any such changes and additional terms as are deemed necessary or appropriate by the authorized signatory.

It currently expires on December 31, 2024 and is valued at $6.84 million.
We are seeking to extend the contract for another year as well as to increase the value by an estimated $500,000.
The contract extension will run from January 1sts through December 31st of 2025.

The current contract extension is still being negotiated and is expected to be between $400,000-$450,000 and no more than $500,000.
We are seeking approval for the maximum amount while negotiations continue.
The estimated increase of $500,000 represents a 7.2% increase in the value of the contract.
It does not materially change the contract and i s for the annual renewal.
The contract represents ongoing support services which are part of the current operations of the campus.
This change order is in line with the annual usage.
